title: Medical Devices and Insulin in Power Cuts
summary: Preserving insulin efficacy, managing electrically powered medical equipment, and emergency escalation.
content:
1. Priority Services Register (PSR):
- Vulnerable residents, medical device users, and elderly citizens should register in advance with the Priority Services Register via UK Power Networks (call 105).
- Registration helps network operators prioritise support during prolonged outages.

2. Electrically Powered Medical Equipment (Oxygen, Ventilators, CPAP, Dialysis):
- Maintain full charges on all backup battery packs.
- Keep manual override tools, manual ambu-bags, or alternative supplies readily accessible.
- If backup power depletes or life-supporting equipment fails, call 999 immediately or arrange prompt transit to the nearest hospital A&E.

3. Insulin Storage Rules:
- Unopened insulin: Stores ideally between 2°C and 8°C. Keep your fridge door closed to maintain cool internal temperature.
- In-use insulin: Safely stays at room temperature (below 25°C to 30°C) for up to 28 days without refrigeration.
- Warm weather management: If indoor temperatures exceed 30°C, place insulin inside an insulated cool bag alongside cold water bottles or wrapped ice packs.
- DO NOT FREEZE: Never allow insulin to touch bare ice or freeze. Discard insulin immediately if it has frozen, as freezing permanently destroys the protein structure.

4. Powered Wheelchairs and Mobility:
- Keep backup power banks charged. Maintain manual release tools nearby so the chair can be pushed manually if battery power fails.
